items.bold: Ghalibaf adviser: Extension "ploy to buy time for a surprise strike." Iran deeply suspicious.
items.text: Ghalibaf's adviser Mahdi Mohammadi (Reuters): called Trump's ceasefire extension "a ploy to buy time" for a surprise strike. Said the US blockade "is no different from bombardment and must be met with a military response." This reflects the dominant IRGC-aligned view within Iran's power structure. Iran's armed forces commander Abdollahi on Tuesday said Iran was "prepared to respond decisively to the enemy's breach of promises." Iranian state TV and IRGC media continue warning that Hormuz will remain closed. The IRGC is not treating the ceasefire extension as a diplomatic opening — they are treating it as a tactical pause before escalation. The IRGC's influence under new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei (more hardline, very close to IRGC) makes this posture likely to persist.

items.bold: NEW IRAN SUPREME LEADER: Mojtaba Khamenei — hardline, IRGC-aligned. Key structural fact.
items.text: CNBC oil timeline article confirmed: Iran named Mojtaba Khamenei — son of the late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei — as its new Supreme Leader. He is described as "more hardline, with very close ties to the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps." This is the single most important structural fact about Iran's negotiating posture: the new Supreme Leader is IRGC-aligned, which means the IRGC's hardline position on negotiations (no talks while blockade continues; Hormuz as sovereign Iranian territory) now has the Supreme Leader's backing. This explains why Ghalibaf and the Foreign Ministry are constrained from making concessions even when they might privately want to. Any deal must be approved by Mojtaba Khamenei — and his IRGC alignment makes the nuclear enrichment and Hormuz issues even harder to resolve.

items.bold: IRAN AIR RESUMING DOMESTIC FLIGHTS TODAY — after 50-day suspension. Partial normalisation signal.
items.text: NBC live blog confirmed: Iran Air announced domestic flights resume today after a 50-day suspension caused by the West Asia War. First service: Tehran to Mashhad, departing this morning with a return flight the same day. This is a meaningful signal — Iran is acting as if it expects the ceasefire to hold and is beginning domestic normalisation. It does not signal diplomatic flexibility on the Hormuz or nuclear issues, but it does suggest Iran is not planning an imminent military escalation that would trigger US strikes. For context: Iran suspended all domestic flights on February 28 when the war began, expecting US strikes on infrastructure including airports. Resuming flights signals Iran calculates the ceasefire is stable enough for civilian aviation.

It does not signal diplomatic flexibility — Iran's military posture and refusal to talk while blockade continues is unchanged. But it does suggest Iran is not planning an imminent offensive that would trigger US retaliation. For India: Iran resuming domestic aviation reduces the probability of sudden West Asia War escalation in the very near term.

military.t: India: Stalemate Means Brent $93-100 for Weeks. LPG/Petrol Relief Still Distant.
military.d: The West Asia War stalemate phase has specific implications for India's energy economy: (1) Brent likely stays $90-100 range for the duration of the stalemate — no immediate crash without Hormuz opening, no spike without new military incident. (2) India's LPG cut that was reversed when Brent rose above $95 will stay reversed — OMCs under margin pressure. (3) Petrol/diesel hike risk: OMCs have been absorbing losses; if stalemate continues 4+ weeks, a Rs 2-5/litre hike becomes likely. (4) India strategic petroleum buffer: 6-8 weeks originally — now consumed for 54 days. India has been drawing on domestic refiners' crude inventories and alternative suppliers (US, Russia, Africa) but the Hormuz supply chain gap is real. (5) Fertiliser: Gulf produces ~30% of global urea — India's Kharif crop season (June-August) planting decisions are now at risk if Hormuz stays closed through May.

assessment.body:
Wednesday 9:30 AM IST. The West Asia War has entered its stalemate phase.

THE STATE OF PLAY — WHAT IS CONFIRMED
• Ceasefire: indefinitely extended, still holding. No new attacks either side
• Hormuz: 12 vessels past 24 hours — mostly Iranian-flagged on Bandar Abbas route. Not zero, not open
• Vance: still in Washington. No departure date set. "Things quite fluid"
• Iran: no delegation sent. Tasnim: Iran NOT attending Wednesday talks
• Ghalibaf adviser: extension "a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike"
• Iran Air: resuming domestic flights today (50-day suspension ends) — calculates ceasefire stable

THE STRUCTURAL KEY — NEW SUPREME LEADER
• Mojtaba Khamenei — son of the late Ayatollah — named as new Supreme Leader
• Described as more hardline with very close ties to the IRGC
• Any deal must receive Supreme Leader sign-off
• IRGC hardline position now has Supreme Leader backing
• This makes nuclear enrichment and Hormuz sovereign control concessions much harder
• The diplomatic corps (Araghchi) is constrained not just by IRGC but by the Supreme Leader himself

WHAT THE STALEMATE MEANS FOR INDIA
• Brent $90-100 range for weeks — no crash, no spike (absent new incident)
• LPG/petrol hike risk: OMCs absorbing losses; Rs 2-5/litre hike likely in 4+ weeks if stalemate continues
• Fertiliser: Gulf produces ~30% global urea; Kharif planting (June-Aug) at risk if Hormuz stays closed through May
• India SPR buffer of 6-8 weeks has been consumed — now dependent on alternative supply lines
• Tifani seizure in Indian Ocean = US enforcement in India's maritime neighbourhood
• 280 Indian seafarers still affected. 8 Indian vessels in region

TODAY'S MARKET FOCUS: INFOSYS Q4
• With ceasefire stable and Brent below $100, India markets shift to fundamentals
• Infosys Q4 FY26 results = primary catalyst
• IT sector has been under pressure; a beat + positive FY27 guidance could be the catalyst to push Sensex toward 80,000
• Sensex 79,273 prev close. VIX expected to ease to 15-17
• FII: power and capital goods accumulation continuing; IT awaits Infosys

THE SCENARIO SHIFT
• Immediate war resumption: ~8% (ceasefire holding, Iran Air resuming flights)
• Deal this week: ~20% (no talks date, IRGC-aligned Supreme Leader)
• Stalemate 4+ weeks: ~60% — most likely. No deadline, no pressure
• Iranian military escalation: ~12% (IRGC warns, but Iran Air resumption suggests restraint for now)

VERDICT: The West Asia War has settled into a grinding stalemate. No bombs. No deal. Hormuz trickling at 10% capacity. The world is learning to live with $95 Brent. India is consuming its buffer daily. And the new Iranian Supreme Leader — more hardline than his father, IRGC through and through — makes the diplomatic gap wider than it was at the start. The immediate question for India's markets this morning: does Infosys deliver a beat that takes Sensex through 80,000?
